Only methods declared in candy-gifview/src, or inherited from a parent declared there, are listed. A type that extends a class outside that tree, such as \RuntimeException, does not show the methods of that class.

SugarCraft\GifView

Cli final class

Command-line entry point: parse argv, size the decode grid to the viewport, hand the frames to sugar-animation's Player, and run the SugarCraft Program.

MethodSummary
static runningVersion(): stringThe version this run reports: the phar archive's build stamp when executing inside one (InstalledVersions lies under the frozen phar vendor/, so the stamp is the only truth), else the compiled-in Support\Version::CURRENT. The archive is identified by \Phar::running(false), which is exactly the real path the \Phar constructor wants here (this class only ever runs required from inside the archive, never as the stub).
static main(array $argv, $stdout, $stderr, ?\Closure $play = null, ?\Closure $watchStat = null, ?\Closure $decode = null): intRun the viewer front end.
static viewportCells(): arraySize the decode grid to the terminal viewport: rows-2, one row for the Player's status line and one for the trailing newline its view() emits — an over-tall final line scrolls the alt screen by one. The COLUMNS/LINES environment pair wins first (bare positive integers — the universal CLI escape hatch for hosts the probe cannot answer); otherwise the never-throwing sugar-core Tty facade probes STDOUT. Off a terminal (piped output, CI) the grid is the deterministic 60x24 fallback. On resize the engine re-clamps to rows-1 itself (sugar-animation Player; engine seam), so the reserve is exact for the initial paint.

Lang final class

Per-library translation facade for candy-gifview.

SugarCraft\GifView\Support

Version final class

Single source of truth for the printed version.

MethodSummary
static resolve(string $archive, string $fallback = self::CURRENT): stringResolve the version for the current run.
static fromPharMetadata(string $archivePath): ?stringRead and normalize the version stamp inside an archive, or null when the path is empty, is not a file, is not a readable phar, or its stamp does not parse as a comparable release. Every failure mode falls back to null rather than throwing — a corrupt archive must not crash --version.
static normalizeStamp(string $stamped): ?stringNormalize a build stamp to a printable version, or null when it names neither a comparable release nor a recognised development identity: TAG_PREFIX stripped, a leading v stripped, then the COMPARABLE release shape, then the DEV grammar. One grammar, one home — the producer (tools/build-phar.php) validates against exactly this rule through isStampable(), so a stamp that would be dropped at runtime is refused at build time instead of silently printing CURRENT.
static isStampable(string $stamped): boolWhether a producer may stamp this string at all (the consumer decides).
